details: Last week's International Monetary Fund and World Bank meetings concluded without new solutions for developing nations grappling with a spreading Middle East conflict, the ongoing war in Ukraine, increasing debt payments, and the potential risks of an AI bubble. These global challenges are leading to higher debt service costs and inflation, making it harder for lower-income countries to keep pace economically.
title: IMF and World Bank Meetings Address Global Economic Headwinds

details: US President Donald Trump has waived legislative provisions that would have allowed for tariffs on nations purchasing significant amounts of Russian crude or aiding Moscow in evading sanctions. This decision coincides with Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to Central Asia, highlighting the region's efforts to diversify international partnerships. India, a major importer of Russian crude, was among the nations that could have been affected by the sanctions.
title: Trump Waives Russian Sanctions, Rubio Visits Central Asia

details: Tensions remain high as families in Gaza face food shortages due to halted commercial shipments. Meanwhile, a Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's St. Petersburg reportedly killed one person and hit energy facilities. In the Middle East, a Singapore-flagged container ship was sunk in the Strait of Hormuz by an Iranian projectile, further intensifying supply disruption concerns in the oil market.
title: Geopolitical Tensions Escalate: Gaza, Ukraine, and Oil Markets

details: A Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll indicates that nearly two-thirds of Americans believe President Donald Trump is using his presidency for personal enrichment, a view increasingly shared by Republican-leaning independents. This sentiment is fueled in part by his family's cryptocurrency and foreign business dealings. Democrats are reportedly preparing to investigate Trump's ties to the crypto industry if they gain control of Congress in the upcoming midterms.
title: Increased Scrutiny on Trump's Crypto Ties Ahead of US Midterms

details: Bitcoin prices have shown volatility, slipping approximately 2% to around $81,700 earlier in the week, following inflation reports. The cryptocurrency market saw nearly $950 million in leveraged positions liquidated, while spot Bitcoin ETFs experienced over $261 million in outflows. However, Bitcoin later rebounded to $82,045. The market remains sensitive to inflation data and the Federal Reserve's interest rate outlook.
title: Bitcoin Experiences Volatility Amid Inflation Concerns
